selectionPolicy: Learning items are editorial selections from the full Watch master. They are not the full script divided into activities.

mimic.text: One winter morning, he discovered a plain block of wood beside his bench.
mimic.selectionReason: A clear scene-setting sentence with useful storytelling rhythm.

mimic.text: Master Cherry rubbed his hands, lifted his axe, and whispered, “This will do nicely.”
mimic.selectionReason: Practises three coordinated actions followed by expressive dialogue.

mimic.text: Before the blade touched the wood, a tiny voice cried, “Please don’t hit me!”
mimic.selectionReason: Carries the Chapter's first surprise and a reusable time clause.

mimic.text: “I must have imagined it,” he decided, though his knees had begun to shake.
mimic.selectionReason: Pairs spoken confidence with physical fear.

mimic.text: A piece of wood could not speak, yet this one clearly had opinions.
mimic.selectionReason: Compact cause of comedy with a high-value contrast pattern.

mimic.text: The moment the tool scraped across it, the wood laughed like a cheeky child.
mimic.selectionReason: Combines precise timing, sound, and characterisation.

mimic.text: At that exact moment, someone knocked loudly at the shop door.
mimic.selectionReason: A versatile suspense connector with strong sentence stress.

mimic.text: Geppetto entered, wearing a patched coat and a hopeful smile.
mimic.selectionReason: Introduces a character through two concise visual details.

mimic.text: He was poor, but his imagination was richer than any king’s treasure room.
mimic.selectionReason: Expresses poverty and inner richness in one memorable line.

mimic.text: “I shall make a wooden boy who can dance, fence, and turn somersaults.”
mimic.selectionReason: States Geppetto's plan with playful three-part rhythm.

mimic.text: More than money, Geppetto wanted company in his small, lonely home.
mimic.selectionReason: Reveals the emotional motive beneath the practical plan.

mimic.text: Before he touched it, the hidden voice called, “Good afternoon, Polendina!”
mimic.selectionReason: Creates comic interruption with a repeatable time pattern.

mimic.text: Their argument became a storm of accusations, stamping feet, and flying insults.
mimic.selectionReason: Turns conflict into a vivid, speakable image.

mimic.text: A moment later, they were rolling across the floor like two angry sacks of flour.
mimic.selectionReason: A physical comic beat with clear rhythm and imagery.

mimic.text: As Geppetto walked home through the narrow streets, he imagined the puppet bowing before a delighted crowd.
mimic.selectionReason: Moves from physical journey to inner hope in one sentence.

mimic.text: He imagined music, applause, and warm meals shared beside the fire.
mimic.selectionReason: A short expressive line built around concrete desires.

mimic.text: A painted fire on the wall had to pretend to keep him warm.
mimic.selectionReason: Shows poverty through one memorable visual sentence.

mimic.text: “Let us make a boy,” he said, “and perhaps a family too.”
mimic.selectionReason: Connects the act of making with the deeper family theme.

mimic.text: The moment the eyes appeared, they stared directly at him.
mimic.selectionReason: A concise magical transformation with strong stress.

mimic.text: The nose grew longer and longer, no matter how often Geppetto shortened it.
mimic.selectionReason: Uses a useful persistence pattern around the iconic nose.

mimic.text: He shaped a mouth, and the mouth immediately began to grin.
mimic.selectionReason: A clean cause-and-reaction sentence for connected speech.

mimic.text: As soon as the hands were finished, they snatched away his yellow wig.
mimic.selectionReason: Pairs a high-value connector with a comic action.

mimic.text: One step became two, and two steps became a wild dash around the room.
mimic.selectionReason: Makes a fast escalation easy to hear and reproduce.

mimic.text: Pinocchio kicked over a stool, leapt across the bed, and raced towards the door.
mimic.selectionReason: Practises energetic past-tense verbs in one visual line.

mimic.text: The puppet pulled the latch and shot into the street.
mimic.selectionReason: A compact escape sentence with a strong final beat.

mimic.text: Freedom felt too exciting, and consequences were still a mystery.
mimic.selectionReason: Summarises Pinocchio's emotional logic without moralising.

mimic.text: Pinocchio tried to slip past, but the constable caught him by his remarkable nose.
mimic.selectionReason: A useful tried-to-but pattern tied to a memorable action.

mimic.text: When he caught the puppet by the neck instead, Pinocchio threw himself onto the road and refused to move.
mimic.selectionReason: Shows the action that causes the crowd to misunderstand Geppetto.

mimic.text: The constable listened to the loudest voices instead of examining the facts.
mimic.selectionReason: A memorable consequence line with a reusable contrast frame.

mimic.text: And somewhere ahead, the wooden boy’s first hard lesson was already waiting.
mimic.selectionReason: Closes the Chapter while pulling the learner into the next one.

guess.cue: Master Cherry raises his axe and hears an impossible warning.

options.text: Before the blade touched the wood, a tiny voice cried, “Please don’t hit me!”
This time, the axe came down, and the voice cried, “Oh! You hurt me!”
At that exact moment, someone knocked loudly at the shop door.

guess.distractorStrategy: Other surprising sounds from the same opening sequence.

guess.cue: The empty shop makes Master Cherry doubt what he heard, even while his body shows fear.

options.text: “There must be a trick,” he muttered.
“I must have imagined it,” he decided, though his knees had begun to shake.
“I have a wonderful plan,” he announced.

guess.cue: The plane touches the block and proves that the wood reacts like a child.

options.text: He searched beneath the bench, behind the door, and inside every cupboard.
The block gave a quiet, satisfied chuckle.
The moment the tool scraped across it, the wood laughed like a cheeky child.

guess.distractorStrategy: One search action and one later laugh compete with the exact reaction.

guess.cue: Geppetto describes the wooden performer he wants to create.

options.text: “I shall make a wooden boy who can dance, fence, and turn somersaults.”
“I shall call you Pinocchio.”
“Stop!” cried Geppetto.

guess.distractorStrategy: Other Geppetto quotations from later actions.

guess.cue: The hidden voice insults Geppetto before he even touches the wood.

options.text: “Friends again,” Master Cherry replied.
Before he touched it, the hidden voice called, “Good afternoon, Polendina!”
“He is my boy, and I shall take him home.”

guess.distractorStrategy: Other dialogue lines with different speakers and intentions.

guess.cue: Geppetto chooses the name that sounds bright and full of adventure.

options.text: “I have a wonderful plan,” he announced.
“Friends again?” Geppetto asked.
“I shall call you Pinocchio.”

guess.cue: Geppetto cannot control the most famous feature of the puppet's face.

options.text: The nose grew longer and longer, no matter how often Geppetto shortened it.
One step became two, and two steps became a wild dash around the room.
Pinocchio tried to slip past, but the constable caught him by his remarkable nose.

guess.cue: Pinocchio opens the way out and begins his first escape.

options.text: As Geppetto walked home through the narrow streets, he imagined the puppet bowing before a delighted crowd.
The puppet pulled the latch and shot into the street.
He released Pinocchio and took Geppetto by the arm.

guess.distractorStrategy: Other street movement or release moments.

guess.cue: The constable makes a bad decision because he follows noise rather than facts.

options.text: Master Cherry lifted both hands and swore it was not him.
“Thank goodness,” he said.
The constable listened to the loudest voices instead of examining the facts.

guess.distractorStrategy: Other reactions that do not express the constable's error.

guess.cue: Geppetto names the painful gap between the love he gave and the judgment Pinocchio lacks.

options.text: “Oh, Pinocchio,” he sighed, “I made you with love, but I forgot to give you sense.”
“Let us make a boy,” he said, “and perhaps a family too.”
“I must have imagined it,” he decided, though his knees had begun to shake.

guess.distractorStrategy: Other emotional dialogue from earlier hopes and fears.
